newsitem.title: SPAIN: Rebel leader warns Peru not to use force in siege.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader warns Peru not to use force in siege.

text.p: The leader of Marxist rebels holding 72 people captive in the home of the Japanese ambassador in Peru warned in an interview on Sunday that any use of force by Peruvian security would end in tragedy for the hostages.
Nestor Cerpa said in an interview with Spanish newspapers El Pais and La Vanguardia he and his followers were prepared to die if Peru resorted to force to end the standoff.
"The assault (by the Peruvian army) will be tragic for the captive gentlemen," Cerpa was quoted as saying.
"If they decide to use force, they will find every one of us prepared for combat. We are aware that if things turn out this way, we will not leave alive."

Cerpa and his MRTA rebels have been demanding the release of imprisoned comrades in return for freedom of the hostages held since December 17. He said the rebels, who originally took 500 hostages then let most go, would not release any more.
Cerpa acknowledged one of his personal motives in the siege is to free his wife Nancy who is among the MRTA prisoners.
"I can't deny that it is one more motive because I love her and I am aware that our children need their mother," he told the newspapers.
